sources.notes: BMW contrasts the road car's six-speed manual with the race M3 GTR's sequential transmission. Exact race gear count and actuation are supported by live testing.

sources.title: BMW M4 GT3 Race Car
sources.notes: Manufacturer page for the M4 GT3: six-speed sequential Xtrac transaxle derived from the M8 GTE, with an electro-hydraulic clutch operated by steering-wheel paddles, no clutch pedal, and stall prevention.

sources.title: Sales launch for the newly developed BMW M4 GT4

sources.title: Gearbox - Syncro vs Dog engagement
sources.notes: Technical comparison stating that a dog box needs perfect rpm selection by the driver or severe damage can be experienced, while synchromesh units make automatic adjustments to match gear and hub speeds. sources.title: 2000 Oreca Viper, chassis C38
sources.notes: Includes a first-person account from Carsport Holland team principal Toine Hezemans that his team replaced the Oreca H-pattern gearbox with a Holinger sequential. sources.title: Academy Championship

sources.title: Anexo Tecnico Plataforma Stock Car Pro Series Car 2024
sources.notes: Official platform annex identifies the common prescribed steering wheel, pedals, transmission, and paddle-shift system used by the 2024 cars.

sources.title: Campeonato Brasileiro de Stock Car Pro Series - Regulamento Tecnico 2024
sources.notes: Official series regulations prescribe the Xtrac 396B023 transmission, semi-automatic paddle-shift actuation, and a multi-disc clutch. In-game technique is verified separately.

sources.title: 2023 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 Elevates the American Supercar
sources.notes: Manufacturer release establishes that Z07 is a Z06 performance package and specifies the eight-speed dual-clutch transmission with shift paddles. Exact AMS2 behavior and rim classification were tested directly.

sources.title: Corvette Racing
sources.notes: Manufacturer motorsport page identifies the Z06 GT3.R's six-speed sequential motorsport transaxle. It does not independently establish AMS2 clutch, cut, or blip behavior.

sources.title: Sebring-winning Panoz Esperante GTLM race car
sources.notes: Specialist motorsport article identifies the period GTLM and its Hewland sequential gearbox. It does not establish gear count, actuation, technique, or wheel shape.

sources.title: Corvette Racing vehicle information
sources.notes: Official racing program information identifies the Corvette Z06 GT3.R's Xtrac six-speed gearbox and provides steering-wheel reference imagery. Simulator actuation and technique are verified separately.

sources.title: 2000 Lister Storm GTM technical specification
sources.notes: Specialist vehicle dossier identifies a Hewland TGTA six-speed sequential gearbox operated by a push-pull lever on a documented 2000 Storm GTM. It supports the hardware family but not every later chassis or the AMS2 technique.

sources.title: 2016 Dodge Viper specifications
sources.notes: Manufacturer press specifications identify the ACR's synchronized six-speed manual and ACR-specific sixth ratio. Gate and technique are supported by live testing.

sources.title: Puma P052 specs and price

sources.title: Formula Vee 2025 Regulamento Geral/Tecnico
sources.publisher: Federacao de Automobilismo de Sao Paulo

sources.title: 575 GTC

sources.title: Audi V8 Quattro homologation record 5409
sources.notes: Official FIA identity and homologation context for the Group A Audi V8 Quattro. Exact gate and simulator technique are established separately.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette homologation form B-260
sources.notes: Official homologation evidence for a related C3-era Corvette shows a floor-shifted Doug Nash manual gearbox, conventional H gate, and hydraulic clutch. It does not uniquely identify Reiza's fictionalized C3.R Convertible or establish its exact control behavior.

sources.title: 2006 Formula One Technical Regulations

sources.title: 2008 Formula One Technical Regulations
sources.notes: Official period regulations cap 2008 Formula One gearboxes at seven forward ratios and describe hydraulic gear-selection actuation. Exact R28 controls come from live testing.

sources.title: Lister Storm homologation record and Homologation Form GT-008
sources.notes: Primary homologation form documents six manual forward ratios and period transmission extensions. It does not unambiguously establish the late GTM actuation or technique.

sources.title: Homologation form number 15, Group GT: Lamborghini Murcielago
sources.notes: Primary homologation evidence for the Murcielago competition identity. The extracted form does not clearly establish driver control technique.

sources.title: Saleen S7 GT Homologation Form GT-013
sources.notes: Primary homologation evidence for the Saleen S7 competition identity and longitudinal gearbox architecture. The visible form does not establish the exact AMS2 gear count, actuation, or driver technique.

sources.title: Formula Vee: o que e e como funciona a categoria
sources.notes: Official category explainer specifies a manual H-pattern transmission for the current Formula Vee. It does not establish the AMS2 clutch, lift, blip, or wheel behavior by itself.

sources.title: F1 Glossary - Gearbox
sources.notes: Official championship explainer supports semi-automatic steering-wheel paddle actuation generally. Exact Renault model behavior remains grounded in the live AMS2 observations.

sources.title: How the 2005 Renault R25 finally ended Ferrari's dominance
sources.notes: Official championship technical history supports the R25 model identity and gearbox context. It does not independently establish the exact forward gear count or user-facing control technique.

sources.title: 2003 Corvette C5-R specifications
sources.notes: Archived General Motors specification listing a six-speed sequential-manual transaxle for the 2003 Corvette C5-R. It does not establish the exact year represented in AMS2 or driver technique.

sources.title: The five best Aston Martin racing cars

sources.notes: Official series overview of the common LMDh hybrid system, including the ability of an LMDh car to move through pits or paddock on electric power alone. Used to interpret the observed clutch-free move-off as hybrid launch behavior rather than a generic auto-clutch aid.

sources.title: Transmission/Gearbox/Shifting Types & Method
sources.notes: Official article used as the design target for the iRacing staging importer. No iRacing records are promoted in dataset 0.1.0.

sources.title: Lamborghini Diablo: celebrating 35 years of an icon
sources.notes: Manufacturer-derived heritage data specifies a five-speed Lamborghini manual plus reverse and a dry single-plate clutch for the Diablo SV-R. It does not establish the dogleg gate or running-shift technique.

sources.title: Huracan GT3 EVO2
sources.notes: Official model page establishes the exact EVO2 identity and provides cockpit and racing-wheel imagery. The parsed text does not independently establish clutch, cut, or blip technique.

sources.title: Lamborghini celebrates 10 years since maiden Huracan GT3 victory
sources.notes: Manufacturer history describes the Huracan GT3 lineage, including EVO and EVO2, with a six-speed sequential gearbox. Exact AMS2 actuation and technique are verified separately.

sources.title: Lamborghini Miura: The first supercar in history
sources.notes: Official Miura family history identifies the SV and a five-speed manual transmission. Exact SV gate and technique come from live testing.

sources.title: Revuelto digital brochure 2024
sources.notes: Manufacturer brochure specifies an eight-gear automated dual-clutch transmission. Exact simulator controls are supported separately.

sources.title: Lamborghini unveils SC63 hybrid racing prototype
sources.notes: Manufacturer announcement identifies the SC63 as an LMDh hybrid using the category's standard transmission architecture. Exact driver technique remains simulator-specific.

sources.title: Lamborghini Super Trofeo Europe 2022 Championship Brochure
sources.notes: Official brochure specifies an Xtrac six-speed sequential racing gearbox, Magneti Marelli electric actuator, lightweight flywheel, and racing clutch. Driver technique remains simulator-specific.

sources.title: Veneno Roadster technical specifications
sources.notes: Official model archive identifies the Veneno Roadster and provides cockpit reference imagery. A related Lamborghini history article specifies the seven-speed ISR architecture; exact AMS2 controls were tested directly.

sources.title: Ligier JS P217 technical specifications
sources.notes: Primary constructor specification identifies a Hewland TLS-200 six-speed sequential gearbox with semi-automatic pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift. It does not establish launch-clutch technique, cut/blip strategy, or the exact wheel-rim category.

sources.title: Ligier JS P320 technical specifications
sources.notes: Primary constructor specification identifies an Xtrac 1152 six-speed sequential gearbox, semi-automatic pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift, and Magneti Marelli gearbox/engine ECUs. Launch and cut/blip technique require separate evidence.

sources.title: Ligier JS P4 technical sheet
sources.notes: Primary constructor specification identifies a six-speed transverse gearbox, wheel-mounted selection, ZF centrifugal twin-disc clutch, and pneumatic shifts. It does not by itself prove AMS2 cut/blip behavior.

sources.title: Ligier JS2 R technical sheet
sources.notes: Manufacturer specification states a six-speed sequential gearbox, centrifugal twin-disc clutch, pneumatic paddle shift, and bespoke integrated-display wheel. Driver technique is established separately.

sources.title: Lola B05/40, B05/42, MG EX264 specifications
sources.notes: Archived constructor-attributed specification stating that the Judd V8, Zytek, and AER turbo installations use six-speed manual sequential gearboxes. It does not establish paddle actuation, start technique, cut/blip, or wheel shape.

sources.title: Lola Heritage - T710 Corvette GTP
sources.notes: Chassis-builder heritage record for the Lola T710 that underpins the Corvette GTP. Used for real-world chassis identity context.

sources.title: Kit 718 GT4 Clubsport MR (982)
sources.notes: Manthey Racing's MR kit for the 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport. The kit revises aerodynamics and suspension and makes no powertrain change, so the six-speed PDK of the base Clubsport is retained.

sources.title: Maserati GranSport brochure
sources.notes: Archived original manufacturer brochure specifies the production GranSport's six-speed electrohydraulic Cambiocorsa gearbox, paddle controls, and simulated heel-and-toe. Race-car continuity is separately checked.

sources.title: Maserati GT2 Stradale - Racing is Life
sources.notes: Manufacturer model page specifies carbon-fibre paddle shifters and a carbon/Alcantara steering wheel with integrated shift lights. Exact gear count and simulator technique are supported separately.

sources.title: Il Tridente issue 32
sources.notes: Manufacturer magazine specifies the GT2 Stradale's eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. Exact AMS2 move-off and cut/blip behavior are supported separately.

sources.title: MC12 Versione Corse
sources.notes: Manufacturer comparison states that the MC12 GT1 used a manually operated sequential gearbox; the road-derived Versione Corse instead used electro-actuated Cambiocorsa. Gear count and technique are verified separately.

sources.title: McLaren 570S GT4
sources.notes: Manufacturer customer-racing page for the 570S GT4: MonoCell II carbon chassis, 3.8 litre twin-turbo V8, and the Oerlikon Graziano seven-speed dual clutch Sequential Shift Gearbox whose electrically actuated wet clutches pre-select the next gear.

sources.title: Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evolution and its DTM homologation
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the 190E 2.5-16 Evolution homologation specials: a dog-leg five-speed Getrag manual with first gear positioned left and rearward, deliberately moved out of the racing shift plane, with a limited-slip differential.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT3
sources.notes: Manufacturer page for the AMG GT3 family: sequential six-speed racing gearbox mounted at the rear axle in transaxle configuration. The GT3 Evo is the updated version of the same car.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT4
sources.notes: Manufacturer page for the AMG GT4: a sequential six-speed racing gearbox in transaxle configuration on the rear axle, pneumatically operated with shift paddles on the steering wheel, behind the AMG 4.0 litre V8 biturbo.

sources.title: Metalmoro - MRX
sources.notes: Constructor page for the MRX customer prototype, successor to the MCR, with a 2016 chassis revision. It states the car accepts diverse engine and transmission options, so no single real-world gearbox is fixed; the AMS2 Duratec P4 is one such configuration.

sources.title: Classic Mini Gearbox
sources.notes: States the 3 synchromesh gearbox was fitted to all Minis between 1959 and 1968, with synchromesh only on 2nd, 3rd and 4th and first gear of the crash engagement type, and that a full synchromesh first gear arrived in 1968.

sources.title: Ginetta G40: race car buying guide
sources.notes: Describes the G40 with adjustable suspension, a five-speed synchromesh gearbox and a 1.8 Ford Zetec engine. Establishes synchromesh construction for the Cup specification.

sources.title: Dodge Viper GTS-R - Catch Me If You Can
sources.author: Don Sherman
sources.notes: Contemporary engineering report corroborating the production-derived Borg-Warner T56 six-speed transmission and documenting the race car's three-disc carbon-carbon clutch.

sources.title: NASCAR 75 Stock Car Evolution
sources.notes: Official series history supplies generation context and notes the Next Gen sequential shifter. It is not treated as proof that Reiza's fictional Gen1/Gen2/Gen3 labels map exactly to NASCAR generations.

sources.title: Caterham 620 R brings extreme to Goodwood
sources.notes: States the 620R uses a six-speed sequential gearbox with flat-shift behind a supercharged two-litre Ford Duratec of 310 bhp.

sources.title: Nissan GT-R NISMO GT3 2018 specification
sources.notes: NISMO customer-racing specification sheet: six-speed sequential transmission with semi-automatic paddle shift as standard equipment, VR38DETT twin-turbo V6.

sources.title: Nissan Heritage Collection - Nissan R89C
sources.notes: Manufacturer heritage record for the 1989 R89C: VRH35 3,496cc DOHC V8, chassis built by Lola Cars International after the switch from March Engineering, and a VGC five-speed transmission. It establishes real-world identity and gear count, not driver technique.

sources.title: ORECA 07 Media Kit
sources.notes: Primary constructor media kit specifies an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox and pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift. It does not establish launch-clutch technique or simulator cut/blip behavior.

sources.title: Gear Sets and Dog Rings for Webster and Hewland Gearboxes
sources.notes: Catalogues dog rings as the engagement component of Hewland gearboxes, listing parts for the Mk-series and LD200. Establishes dog-ring engagement as Hewland's design approach, though it does not name the DG300 specifically.

sources.title: New Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport featuring natural-fibre body panels
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official launch material for the 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport: a 3.8 litre flat six driving the rear wheels through a Porsche dual-clutch gearbox with six gears. A PDK has no clutch pedal, so the car cannot require clutch input to move off in the real world.

sources.title: Strong, swift, spectacular: the new 911 GT3 R
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official launch material for the 2019 (991.2) 911 GT3 R: Porsche sequential six-speed constant-mesh gearbox with electronic shift actuator, changed by steering-wheel paddles.

sources.title: Debut for the newest generation of the Porsche 911 GT3 R
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official launch material for the 992-generation 911 GT3 R: sequential six-speed constant-mesh gearbox derived from the 911 GT3 Cup, with paddles driving an electronic shift drum actuator.

sources.title: Porsche 911 RSR (2019 model year)
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Manufacturer media guide for the 2019 911 RSR: a weight-optimised six-speed sequential constant-mesh gearbox in magnesium casing, shifted by an electronic actuator through steering-wheel paddles.

sources.title: Porsche 963 | Porsche Motorsport
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official Porsche Motorsport page for the 963 LMDh (Porsche 9RD V8, spec Xtrac seven-speed, 2023 debut). Used for real-world identity context.

sources.title: Gillet Vertigo - only remaining FIA GT chassis
sources.notes: Specialist race-car dossier documents a surviving 2005-period Vertigo with a Tractive six-speed sequential gearbox. It does not establish lever actuation, technique, or wheel shape.

sources.title: Le Mans 2010: Saleen
sources.notes: Specialist technical article specifying an Xtrac six-speed sequential transmission for a 2010 S7-R and stating that the type was introduced in 2002. It supports the family but does not prove the exact 2005 revision or technique.

sources.title: 2005 Spyker C8 GT2-R, chassis 046
sources.notes: Chassis-specific auction listing stating that the 2005 works car used a Hewland six-speed sequential gearbox. It does not establish actuation, technique, cut/blip, or wheel shape.

sources.title: VW Transaxle
sources.notes: States the transmission gears are of the constant-mesh type with balk ring synchronizers, and places the 1st/2nd and 3rd/4th synchronizers on the pinion and main shafts. Establishes the Beetle transaxle as fully synchronized.

sources.title: Technical Data — REITER Lamborghini Murcielago R-GT
sources.notes: Constructor technical data specifies a Hollinger M6S six-speed sequential gearbox and a three-plate Sachs racing clutch. It does not establish driver technique or wheel shape.

sources.title: BMW M6 GT3: 50 Years of Motorsport
sources.notes: The transmission engineer's own account of the M6 GT3 transaxle: a semi-automatic transverse unit with a sequential six-speed plus reverse racing gearbox in a magnesium casing, paddle shifted.

sources.title: Could This Be the Final Front-Engine V-12 Competition Ferrari Ever Made?
sources.notes: Chassis-specific specialist feature describing a six-speed Xtrac sequential stick and showing the cockpit of a Ferrari 575 GTC. It is contextual evidence only; it does not prove the fictional Milano mapping.

sources.title: 2005 Maserati GranSport Trofeo
sources.notes: Chassis-specific dossier with manufacturer correspondence states a six-speed paddle-shift automated manual and three-spoke Momo wheel. Exact modeled technique is tested separately.

sources.title: 1996 Chrysler Viper GTS-R, chassis GTSR C3
sources.notes: Documented chassis history and cockpit photography used as visual evidence for a round racing wheel. The restored early chassis does not by itself establish every late privateer detail.

sources.notes: SimHub 9.11.22 generated .shcarsettings files for locally observed AMS2 cars. The audit found 192 unique identities, with CarId equal to CarModel in every file. Used only to support exact observed telemetry names and explicitly reviewed aliases.

sources.notes: Exact CarModel and CarId values emitted by AMS2 1.6.9.91 and observed through SimHub 9.11.22 during local live tests. These observations support identity matching only; control behavior remains verified against the separately versioned control source.

sources.title: Porsche 911 GT3 RSR (996), 2004-2005
sources.notes: Marque-specialist model history specifying a six-speed sequential gearbox with ignition cut for full-throttle upshifts. It does not establish actuation, start clutch, automatic blip, or wheel shape.

sources.title: 2008 Caterham Seven R500 Superlight
sources.notes: Lists a 6 Speed Caterham Gearbox and states the power is transmitted by either the standard six-speed gearbox or the optional Caterham Motorsport engineered sequential transmission.

sources.title: 10 Iconic Cars with Dogleg Transmissions
sources.notes: Secondary reference describing the dogleg layout and the cars that used it, including the BMW M1's ZF five-speed with first gear out of the natural shift plane.

sources.title: 1970-1980 Puma GTE
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the Brazilian Puma GTE built between 1970 and 1980: fibreglass body on Volkswagen running gear with an air-cooled flat four and a four-speed manual gearbox. sources.title: Manual stick shift system confirmed for Gen3
sources.notes: The championship's own confirmation that Gen3 cars retain the manual gear-change mechanism on the six-speed sequential transaxle, so the category is shifted by a lever rather than paddles.

sources.title: Touring Car Tyros: BMW E30 M3 and Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16
sources.notes: Secondary comparison of the two Group A rivals, recording the E30 M3's Getrag 265 five-speed dogleg manual and limited-slip differential alongside the 190E's dog-leg Getrag.

sources.title: 2004 Birmingham Motor Show Press Information
sources.notes: Archived original manufacturer press kit connecting the T400R platform to the Le Mans program and describing a TVR six-speed sequential gearbox for the model family. It does not unambiguously establish the exact 2005 race-car technique.

sources.title: 5-Speed Gearbox Variants

sources.notes: Lists the Type 9 five-speed in synchronized variants and one unsynchronized dog-engagement variant described as a motorsport application only purists find suitable for road use. Used as the falsifying alternative for the Caterham gearbox inference.

sources.title: Audi R8 (LMP)
sources.notes: Secondary summary describing a six-speed Ricardo sequential transmission with electropneumatic paddle shift. Retained as provisional historical context pending a primary technical replacement; simulator technique and wheel details are sourced separately.

sources.title: BMW M1

sources.title: Brabham BT26
sources.notes: States that the BT26A switched to the Ford-Cosworth DFV and that both variants used a Hewland DG 300, 5-speed manual transmission with a ZF differential, raced from 1968 to 1971.

sources.title: Brabham BT52
sources.notes: Gives the BT52 a Brabham/Hewland 5/6-speed manual with a Weismann differential behind the BMW M12/13 turbocharged four, raced in the 1983 Formula One World Championship.

sources.title: Caterham 7
sources.notes: Lists the Supersport (2011-2014) with a Caterham-Ford Sigma engine, and Seven transmissions as 5-speed manual, 6-speed manual and 6-speed sequential manual. The five-speed manual is therefore the non-sequential option.

sources.title: Caterham Academy
sources.notes: States the Academy package uses a sealed Ford Sigma engine and 5-speed gearbox, and that a six-speed Mazda MX-5 gearbox replaces it for 2026. Establishes the gear count, not the gearbox construction.

sources.title: Chevrolet Chevette
sources.notes: Brazilian Chevette built 1973 to 1993 with 4/5-speed manual gearboxes; a five-speed manual became available as an option on the 1.6 from 1983.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette C8.R
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the C8.R: naturally aspirated LT6.R 5.5 litre V8 and a bespoke compact Xtrac P529 six-speed sequential transaxle, packaged to free room for the rear diffuser.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette GTP
sources.notes: IMSA GTP prototype (Lola T710 chassis, Chevrolet power) raced 1985-1989; Hewland VGC five-speed racing gearbox. Used for real-world identity and gearbox context.

sources.title: Chevrolet Omega
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the Omega used in Stock Car Brasil from 1994 to 1999. The 1999 cars retained a heavily modified straight six derived from the 1979 Opala rather than the V8 introduced in 2001, and 1999 was the last season built on production-car chassis. It does not document the gearbox.

sources.title: Copa Truck
sources.notes: Brazilian racing-truck championship descended from Formula Truck. States the trucks have 1,000 horsepower, twice that of an average transport truck, and brake from over 200 km/h. Lists the competing manufacturers as Ford, Iveco, MAN, Mercedes-Benz, Scania, Volvo and Volkswagen. It gives no gearbox detail.

sources.title: Courage C60
sources.notes: Secondary summary identifying the C60/Hybrid family with a six-speed Xtrac sequential gearbox. Retained as provisional family context pending a primary source; it does not establish exact actuation or technique.

sources.title: Dallara SP1
sources.notes: Secondary model history describing an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox and a 2005 Rollcentre paddle-shift conversion. Retained as provisional context pending a primary technical replacement; exact modeled actuation is resolved by live animation.

sources.title: Fiat Uno
sources.notes: Lists 4- or 5-speed manual transmissions for the first-generation Uno, notes cars built from 1985 to late 1987 used a Ritmo/Strada-derived five-speed gearbox, and dates Brazilian production from 1984.

sources.title: Ginetta G40
sources.notes: Distinguishes the variants: the race G40 Challenge moved from a 5-speed gearbox to 6-speed Quaife sequential gearboxes, while the G40R road car uses the six-speed Mazda MX-5 manual.

sources.title: Ginetta G55
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the G55 family: the GT3 uses a Ginetta Racing 4.35 litre V8 from 2012 with a Hewland six-speed. The article does not differentiate the GT3 gearbox type from the Cup car's sequential manual, and its paddle-shift description belongs to the later G55 GTA.

sources.title: Lotus 49
sources.notes: Specifies a Hewland-Lotus 5-speed manual gearbox with the Ford Cosworth DFV, and dates the 49C from 1969 through its final appearances in 1971.

sources.title: Lotus 98T
sources.notes: Gives the 1986 Lotus 98T a Lotus / Hewland 6-speed manual behind the Renault Gordini EF15B turbocharged V6, driven by Ayrton Senna and Johnny Dumfries.

sources.title: McLaren MP4/1
sources.notes: Gives the 1983 MP4/1C a McLaren / Hewland FGA 400 5-speed manual behind the Ford-Cosworth DFV, before the late-season switch to TAG-Porsche turbo power.

sources.title: Metalmoro JLM AJR
sources.notes: Brazilian sports prototype by Metalmoro (2017); Chevrolet LS3 V8 option, Xtrac 1152 sequential six-speed. Used for real-world identity and gearbox context.

sources.title: Nissan R390 GT1
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the 1998 GT1 car: twin-turbo 3.5 litre V8 driving the rear wheels through an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox operated by a short-throw gear lever, which matches the lever observed in the cockpit rather than paddles.

sources.title: Porsche 911 GT1
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the 911 GT1-98: carbon monocoque, water-cooled 3.2 litre flat six derived from the 962, and a new six-speed sequential gearbox fitted for 1998 to reduce shift time.

sources.title: Porsche 962
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the Group C 962C designation and a five-speed manual transmission. It does not establish synchromesh versus dog engagement or the shift pattern, which remain unknown.

sources.title: Puma GTB
sources.notes: Brazilian road car built 1973 to 1984 with a 4.1-litre Chevrolet 250 inline-six and a 4-speed manual gearbox, with a luxurious touring interior.

sources.title: Volkswagen Gol
sources.notes: First-generation Gol from 1980. Early air-cooled cars used a four-speed manual; of the Gol GT 1.8 (1984-1986) it states the first series still had a four-speed manual gearbox, but soon this was changed to a five-speed unit.

sources.title: Volkswagen Passat (B1)
sources.notes: States the Passat B1 was produced in Brazil from 1974 until 1988 and that improvements from the B2 platform were introduced during its life cycle, including the 1.6 and 1.8-litre engines and a five-speed gearbox.

sources.title: Yamaha FJR1300
sources.notes: Specifies the FJR1300 as a 1,298 cc transverse inline-four with a 5-speed manual gearbox, becoming 6-speed from 2016. Aussie Racing Cars use second-hand FJR1300 engines, so the donor units are the five-speed generation.

sources.title: P1334 NASCAR Transaxle
sources.notes: Supplier specification identifies the real NASCAR Next Gen five-speed manual sequential-change transaxle. Applicability to Reiza Stock USA Gen3 is treated as context and explicitly caveated.

sources.title: P1359 Transverse LMDh Gearbox
sources.notes: Primary supplier specification for the common LMDh transmission: seven-speed sequential, pneumatic integrated-valve gear actuation, and an integrated Bosch motor-generator driving through the gearbox. Hardware architecture alone does not prove AMS2 cut or blip behavior.
